name: @stonedogcode/mobile-auth
description: Phone-side authentication helpers for Expo apps: PKCE and 'connect a phone' codes, an on-device P-256 key unlocked by the fingerprint, and session storage with single-flight refresh. Pairs with @stonedogcode/auth on the server.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//exports: Each optional capability is its own entry point so the core never imports its peers: '.' needs nothing, './expo' needs expo-crypto, './device-key' needs @noble/curves, './expo-device-key' needs expo-secure-store and expo-local-authentication, './expo-session-storage' needs expo-secure-store. An app installs only the peers for the entries it imports.

scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run test:coverage && npm run test:integration && npm run build && npm run verify:package

//publish:stonedog-mobile-auth: Run from a terminal, interactively: npm prompts for the 2FA one-time password and the login flow needs a browser. It refuses a checkout that is detached, dirty, or behind origin/main; refuses a version already published; refuses any runtime dependency, or expo-crypto as anything but an optional peer; refuses shipped source that is not Hermes-safe; refuses a tarball missing an entry point, README, LICENSE or NOTICE, or containing tests. Then it proves the result by installing from the registry into a temp directory and checking that installing alone pulls in no Expo.
//release: One memorable command per repo, as in every other @stonedogcode package. It cannot be called `publish`: that is a reserved npm lifecycle name, so `npm publish` inside scripts/publish-package.sh would fire it and publish a second time. release:dry-run runs every check and stops before npm publish.
//dependencies: None at runtime, deliberately. This sits on the sign-in path of every app that adopts it, so it should be auditable in an afternoon; every dependency it takes, every consumer inherits.
//peerDependencies: All optional, each needed only by the entry point that imports it (see //exports). @noble/curves is audited, pure JS and has no runtime dependency beyond @noble/hashes.
